# telegram-client

> Stand-alone Telegram client layer for Laravel (PHP >= 8.2) on top of the
> teleproto MTProto engine: raw TL updates ingested into idempotent,
> tenant-scoped Postgres truth (anchor/instance/child rows + Eloquent
> models + DTOs generated from the official layer schema), a Redis
> Streams bus with hot-reload routing, a sync multi-account daemon,
> quota-aware history backfill, and encrypted Telegram-channel backup
> vaults. MIT.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md) — package overview
- docs/quickstart.md: 4 first recipes (ingest, route, backfill, backup)
- docs/ingest.md](docs/ingest.md) — ingest API, route semantics, idempotency, tenancy
- [docs/bus.md](docs/bus.md) — Redis stream schema, routing, consumer, daemon, backfill
- [docs/backup.md](docs/backup.md) — encrypted channel vault: crypto, CLI, verifier, limits
- [../teleproto/skills/telegram-methods](../teleproto/skills/telegram-methods) — per-method skill files for the underlying engine (dev checkout sibling)

## Quickstart

```bash
composer require merezarezaei/telegram-client   # engine dep: merezarezaei/teleproto
# provider auto-discovered; config merges from the package — override by
# creating config/telegram-client.php in the host app
```

Ladder position: **teleproto is the engine** (MTProto wire, sessions, pollers,
typed RPC exceptions); **this package is the client layer** — storage truth,
bus, supervision, backfill, backup. It never speaks the wire itself; every
live call goes through teleproto's `UserAccountScope`, and the live wire stays
behind teleproto's tri-state flag (`TELEPROTO_LIVE=true` plus
`TELEGRAM_API_ID`/`TELEGRAM_API_HASH`).

Environment (see `config/telegram-client.php`):

- `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_REDIS` — bus redis driver, `predis` (default) or `phpredis`; bus reads/writes through the host app's `bus.connection` (default `default`)
- `TELEGRAM_SESSION_<ACCOUNT_ID>` — one session string per polled account (credentials: env/secrets only)
- `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_BACKFILL_BUDGET` — backfill request budget (default 25)
- `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_BACKUP_DRIVER` — `memory` (default, offline) or `telegram`; `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_BACKUP_ACCOUNT` (daemon.accounts id), `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_BACKUP_CHUNK_SIZE` (4 MiB), `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE`
- `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_SHIP_NAMESPACES` — override the curated migration dial (default `auth,messages,users,channels,updates,help,contacts`)
- `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_LIVE=1` — gates the live smoke test (`tests/Backup/LiveVaultSmokeTest.php`)

## API

Everything is resolved from the container (singletons bound by the provider):

```php
$client = app(MeRezaRezaei\TelegramClient\TelegramClient::class);

// Updates ALWAYS become instances — they never touch routes.
$root = $client->ingest($updateArray, $accountId);            // : TlInstanceModel

// Method responses are route-deduped per (method, sorted-JSON params, account).
$msgs = $client->ingestResponse('messages.getHistory', $params, $response, $accountId);

// Entity lookup by (tenant, telegram id); null when unseen or deleted.
$user = $client->user($accountId, 501558149);                 // : ?TlUser
$user?->currentInstance->first_name;
$chat = app(EntityAggregator::class)->chat($accountId, $id);   // also ->channel(): same Chat-namespace truth
```

- `UpdateStored` event (`Ingest\Events\UpdateStored`: committed root model + `accountId`) fires after the root transaction commits — once per actual write pass; route-dedup-skipped responses do not re-fire it. Handlers belong to your app.
- Bus (`src/Bus`): `RedisStreamSink` (a teleproto `UpdateSinkInterface`) appends canonical `{account_id, update, ts}` entries to stream `tg:stream:updates`; `IngestConsumer::consumeOnce()` drains batches — route match → forwarded verbatim to the target stream; no match → `TelegramClient::ingest` (an ingest-path failure is retried, cap 3, then dead-lettered with `reason=ingest-failed` + the error message); undecodable poison → `tg:stream:dead-letter` on first sight; everything acked. `RouteTable` (`tg:bus:routes` hash) matches prefix-only (trailing `*`, first pattern in hash order); `HotReloadRouter` re-reads it on `tg:bus:reload` pings (`listen()`) or on `refresh()`.
- Consumer CLI: `php artisan telegram-client:ingest [--once] [--max=N]` — 100 ms idle backoff, graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT, exit 0.
- Daemon (`src/Daemon`): `Daemon` supervises `AccountWorker`s round-robin — 30 s tick per account, FloodWait → interruptible sleep, DC migration → scope rebuild at the new DC, 3 consecutive no-progress failures → account isolated on a 2/5/15/60 s ladder; every account maxed → exit 1 (init system revives). Accounts come from `config('telegram-client.daemon.accounts')` (`{account_id, session_string, dc?, api_id?, api_hash?}`); persist `AccountWorker::lastSequenceState()` (`{pts, date, qts, seq}`) and pass it back as the resume ctor arg. The daemon contains no redis — the bootstrap injects the sink.
- Backfill: `php artisan telegram-client:backfill --account=<id> --peer=@a [--peer=@b] [--budget=25]` — quota rule: a run issues at most `intdiv(budget, 2)` requests (50 % of the budget always reserved for live traffic); every fetch consumes budget; FLOOD_WAIT sleeps `min(seconds, 3600)`; 5 consecutive failures mark the peer dead. Pages land via plain `ingest` (not route-deduped); v1 is report-only (resume from the printed `offset_id`).
- Backup CLI: `php artisan telegram-client:backup <run|restore|verify|prune|status> --set=default [--passphrase=...] [--target=DIR] [--sample=5]` — content-addressed 4 MiB chunks (plaintext sha256), Argon2id13 key derivation + XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretstream per chunk, manifest posted last, manifest-first restore with traversal-proof paths; keyless `verify` samples chunk availability, `--passphrase` upgrades it to full decrypt + hash; `prune` GCs chunks outside the latest manifest's keep-set (keyless, cron-safe after every `run`). `memory` driver is offline-only; `telegram` needs a dedicated session registered in `daemon.accounts`.

## Capabilities

- Storage truth: every payload becomes **anchor / instance / child** rows (shared UUIDv7 PK anchor↔instance, per-constructor instance tables, vector child tables) plus per-method **route** tables for response dedup; all generated from the committed layer-227 `.tl` mirror — Eloquent models, spatie DTOs, factories included.
- Tenancy: every ingest call requires `account_id`; identities resolve per tenant — same telegram id under two accounts is two anchors, two instance sets. No cross-tenant reads.
- Idempotency: re-ingesting an identical update is byte-stable (fill-only upserts, content aggregation); constructor transitions (user → userEmpty) reuse the anchor family; `currentInstance` resolves the latest non-deleted constructor.
- One Redis stream fans in all accounts (multi-account daemon), hot prefix routing fans updates out to app-specific streams without restarts.
- sqlite (in-memory, logic tests) and Postgres (production truth, native uuid + deferrable FKs) from the same generated migrations; bottom-up write order satisfies immediate FKs on both. The PG-only half is exercised by the opt-in PG track (`tests/Pg`, `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_PG=1` — full 637-migration mirror + deferrable-FK proof) and a dedicated CI pg job (postgres:17).

## Constraints

- Sync PHP only: no event loop, no amphp — the daemon is a round-robin supervisor; long waits are chunked interruptible sleeps.
- Curated migration dial: `migrations/` ships **112** of the **635** generated migrations (dial namespaces above); the full mirror always stays in `generated/migrations/`. Extend the dial, never hand-edit generated files — regenerate (`php bin/regenerate --ship`).
- Handlers and business logic belong to the host app; this package emits Laravel events (`UpdateStored`) and stores truth — no handler DSL.
- Zero `preg_*()` in `src/` (phpstan-disallowed-calls gate); string functions and sscanf only.
- Session strings are credentials — never committed; tests never require real credentials. Live tests run only behind `TELEGRAM_CLIENT_LIVE=1` with a real session.
